prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, three-quarter-length demi statue portrait, four-wedge fan-sliced multi-material body, every seam physically stepped, no bare skin below the collarbones. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually finished thigh tips right at the knee, where the leg would bend, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Chinese woman in weixun makeup — clear fair skin, a warm rose-red wash blended across the outer corners of both eyes and drifting up toward the temples, the same flush spreading softly across the cheekbones and the bridge of the nose, slightly smudged, dewy highlights, soft brown-pink eyeshadow, large moist eyes with bright real catchlights and a faint glassy shine, moist rose-tinted lips, long black hair loosely tousled with a few strands across the face, a dreamy, half-lidded expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a big rose-gold hoop hangs clear of the neck down to the shoulder.

Physique: A colossal rounded chest, an enormous belly of massive rounded folds hanging low and heavy, no waist at all, her body a four-wedge fan, three-quarter-length

Boundary: a single straight, flat line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones, never jagged, never zigzag — real skin above, material immediately below, no skin anywhere lower. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step, casting a crisp shadow. Below this line, there is no bare skin anywhere on her body below this line — every part, without exception, is one of the materials described.

Her whole body below the collarbones is divided into four wedge-shaped slices meeting at her chest centre: slice 1 (left arm/shoulder) solid transparent golden-yellow citrine crystal crystal; slice 2 (right arm/shoulder) carved vivid sky-blue turquoise with dark matrix veining, completely opaque; slice 3 (left hip/leg) a glass vessel of clear rose-pink water with drifting rose petals; slice 4 (right hip/leg) carved dark wenge wood with fine gold-tan pinstripes, completely opaque. At every seam where two pieces meet, one edge rises very slightly above its neighbour, casting a thin, crisp shadow — proving each piece is a truly separate object, not a flat pattern painted on one surface. Right at the knee, where the leg would bend, her left thigh seals shut into its own small, smooth, rounded, closed tip (the same rose-pink vessel slice); her right thigh rounds off into its own small, smooth, satin-polished carved tip (the same wenge wood slice).

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a warm golden amber on one side and a deep charcoal grey on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body, the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so amber light glances off one side and grey light glances off the other, catching a crisp glint along every stepped seam. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
